skill_entry.name: 14. An added symbol, include, parameter, branch or header edit needs a consumer at HEAD (and a declaration needs a definition)
skill_entry.trigger: Any one, taken from `git diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src t` (BASE = the PR's base.sha): (a) an added column-0 declaration: `constexpr TYPE NAME =`, a function body `TYPE NAME(` whose line ends in `{` or an open parameter list (not `;`), `using NAME =`, `extern ... NAME(`, or a member added inside a struct the diff touches; (b) an added `#include`, or a removed function body that leaves a bare prototype; (c) a hunk that adds a parameter line under an `@@` context naming a function; (d) an added `if (X)` on a flag or enum inside a block an enclosing `if (X)` / `if (!X)` ... `else` already guards; (e) a statement after `TRON_ASSERT(false`, `std::unreachable` or `abort(`, or a second `TRACE_EVENT_END`, unlock or release for one span in one function; (f) a declaration in the 5 lines above `#ifdef X`; (g) a touched header no other file under h/, src/, t/, bin/ or ingest/ includes.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. Names (a): `git grep -n -w NAME HEAD -- h src t bin ingest`, minus the declaration and definition lines. Zero = item. A member: zero reads outside the struct. 2. Zero-caller function: grep the 10 lines of comment above it for 'called (between|after|before)|reset|clear|release'; a hit sends you to the lifecycle code and to every writer of the fields it clears. 3. Prototype without definition: with call sites = link error (Normal); without = declaration ahead of its code (minor). 4. Include X in file F: list the names X provides (fixed table for standard headers, namespace prefix for out-of-tree headers, grep for in-tree headers); grep F for them outside the include line; compare with BASE:F (already used there = the include added nothing); `git log --no-merges BASE..HEAD -- F` for a move-out commit; `uniq -d` for duplicates, blamed on the commit that added the second copy. 5. Parameter (c): the argument at every call site and the later writer of the field it fills. 6. Branches and statements (d, e, f): walk the enclosing conditions by hand; TRON_ASSERT is unconditional. 7. Includers per touched header (g). 8. Lift test on the title and body; fold minor-tier items into one 'fwiw' line on a lift PR. 9. One item per name; chain 'and this?' under the first.
skill_entry.question: Which line at HEAD, other than its own declaration, reads, calls, includes or compiles this, and if none does, what is it in the PR for?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A test-only or debug-only helper: ask for the label, not removal ('this `xfer_k_entry` is a UT-only utility function. We should document that clearly', 3866590750). A kept-for-later function once the author says so (PR 1920 approved with both dump functions present). A return after an always-failing assert when the author answers it mirrors the old logic (Wade asked 3120804824; author replied 3125423449; not pressed). An include the PR body names with its reason ('header hygiene (<cmath>, <cstdlib>)', PR 2646). Dead code outside the diff (another branch, a pre-existing file): 'fwiw' only (2941308844, 3866653656). Commented-out lines (separate nit). .py, .json, .txt, CMake test rows, doc and register-map regenerations. Helpers of a new test file. Lift PR (title or body says 'step N', 'phase N', 'lifts', 'pulls in', 'from the X branch'): minor-tier items fold into one 'fwiw' line; normal-tier items still fire (3029165954 is on 'phase 1' PR 2287). A member with readers that duplicates a sibling belongs to redundant-code-simplify.
skill_entry.finding_shape: "I don't see where `<name>` is used? (<file>:<line>; at <HEAD> `git grep -w <name>` finds only the declaration.) <left over from <the move to <new file> | the merge> | just for completion/future enhancement?>" and, when the name or comment promises a behaviour: "how come I don't see this being called anywhere? We should be <clearing these flags> <between forward passes> right?" For an include whose names BASE already used: "what does this #include get us?" On a lift PR, one line: "fwiw, <names> have no consumer at this head; they exist on <source branch>, so I assume they land with the next step?"
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: Never 'nit' for this check; always a question. Minor when the leftover compiles to nothing: an unused include, alias, constant, a prototype with neither definition nor caller, or a kept-for-later function ('Just for completion/future enhancement?', 'left over cruft', 'don't need this bf16.hpp include now right?', 'what does this #include get us?'). Normal when a missing consumer means a missing behaviour or a missing definition: 'how come I don't see this being called anywhere? We should be clearing these flags between forward passes right?', 'where's the actual implementation for this now?' (five call sites, no definition), 'if we always call `fill_attn_job_template` with an empty set for 'shards' vector, what's the point?'. Informational ('fwiw') for dead code outside the diff and for minor-tier items on a lift PR.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk; full file (enclosing conditions, the whole include block, the function body for a second end/release); callers (git grep over h/ src/ t/ bin/ ingest/ at HEAD and at BASE for an include's names); other files (the header the PR shrank, the new file the code moved to, the callee of a new parameter, CMakeLists.txt for a new definition file); commits (the move-out commit of F, the commit that added a duplicate include, merge commits); PR title and body only for the lift test and for an include's stated reason. Not CI, not runtime. Line numbers come from the comment's original commit, not the corpus `commit` field.

final.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: an added symbol, include, parameter, branch or header edit needs a consumer at HEAD

Setup. `BASE=$(gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .base.sha)`. When gh is unavailable and HEAD is a merge commit of the base branch, `BASE=$(git -C WT rev-parse HEAD^2)`. Verify with `git -C WT diff --shortstat BASE HEAD` against the PR's changed_files/additions/deletions from `gh api` (PR 1920: 8 files, +1742 -29 at b604cb860a). Never use `git merge-base HEAD origin/<base_ref>` for a merged PR: it returns HEAD (PR 1920, PR 2233) and every step then finds nothing.

1. Added declared names.
   Constants: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src t | grep -oE '^\+\s*(inline\s+)?(static\s+)?constexpr\s+[A-Za-z_0-9:]+\s+[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*' | awk '{print $NF}' | sort -u`.
   Function definitions (column 0 only; the character class must not contain a space, comma or digit, or indented statements and local `std::vector<T> name(n)` declarations match): `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -E '^\+(inline |static )?[A-Za-z_:<>]+ [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*\(' | grep -vE ';\s*$' | grep -oE '[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*\(' | tr -d '(' | sort -u`. Drop names that `git -C WT grep -n -w "$n" BASE -- h src t bin` already finds; only functions the PR introduces remain.
   Aliases and externs over h, src and t (not h alone, or `using json = nlohmann::json;` in t/t_hwattention.cpp is never listed): `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src t | grep -E '^\+\s*(using [A-Za-z_]+ =|extern )'`.
   Struct members: read each touched struct in `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE` and take the added member lines by hand (no grep separates members from locals). A member that has readers but duplicates a sibling (nshards next to shards.size(), 3010846319) belongs to redundant-code-simplify, not here.
2. Consumers per name, declaration excluded: `for n in NAMES; do c=$(git -C WT grep -n -w "$n" HEAD -- h src t bin ingest | grep -v -E "constexpr [A-Za-z_0-9:]+ $n *=" | wc -l); printf "%-28s consumers=%s\n" "$n" "$c"; done`. For a function also use `-w` and subtract the definition line and the prototype line, when one exists; do not use `NAME\s*\(` (a9a9cf30a4:h/tron/models/model.hpp:2825 `base_load` has 4 uses by `-w`, 0 by the paren form). consumers=0 is an item. For a member list writers too; a writer the diff deletes, or that only mirrors a superseded field, counts as dead.
3. Promise in the comment of a zero-consumer function: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n "$((L-10)),${L}p" | grep -n -i -E 'called (between|after|before|on|when)|reset|clear|release|must be|should be'`. Only a hit sends the item to the lifecycle search: grep the point the comment names (`git -C WT grep -n -E 'forward pass|reuse|create_children' HEAD -- h/tron/scheduler h/tron/models`) and every writer of the fields the function writes (`git -C WT grep -n 'k_complete_\|v_complete_' HEAD -- h src`). A Doxygen block without a hit (dump_kv_cache_from_hbm, 2d53016b44:h/pos/hwattention.hpp:1135-1144) stays minor from step 2.
4. Declaration without definition: `for n in EXTERN_NAMES; do git -C WT grep -n -E "^[A-Za-z].* $n\(" HEAD -- src h; done`; `git -C WT grep -n '<defining file>' HEAD -- 'src/*/CMakeLists.txt'`; confirm the defining file is in `git -C WT ls-tree HEAD <path>`. No definition at HEAD and none at BASE: if `git -C WT grep -n -w "$n" HEAD -- h src t bin ingest` finds a call site, it is a link error, Normal ('where's the actual implementation for this now?', 3463077403: five call sites, no definition; 4d2a3951e7 adds `models/hw_attn_config.cpp` to src/tron/CMakeLists.txt while the file is absent from the tree, d71d7cfc13 adds it two days later). No call site either: the declaration is ahead of its code, minor; on a lift PR it goes into the one 'fwiw' line (7f993bc2db:h/tron/hardware/driver.hpp:231, :246, :331, :337, :344 on PR 1707, Wade silent).
5. Added includes: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD | grep -E '^\+\+\+ |^\+#include'`. Per include X in file F:
   Names X provides, three cases. (a) Standard header, fixed table: <fstream> -> ifstream, ofstream, fstream; <thread> -> std::thread, this_thread, jthread; <atomic> -> atomic; <exception> -> std::exception, terminate, rethrow; <random> -> mt19937, random_device, uniform_; <cmath> -> std::abs, isnan, isinf, sqrt, pow, exp, log, floor, ceil, round; <cstdlib> -> getenv, malloc, free, abs, strtol; <cstdint> and <cstddef> never a finding. (b) Header not in the tree (spdlog, fmt, catch2, nlohmann): grep F for the namespace prefix the header owns (`fmt::`, `spdlog::`, `nlohmann::`, `Catch::`). (c) In-tree header: `git -C WT show HEAD:X | grep -oE '^(extern |inline |constexpr |static |template)?[A-Za-z_:<>*& ]+ [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*\(' | grep -oE '[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*\($' | tr -d '('`, plus `^(struct|class|using|namespace) NAME`, plus the namespace of every `#include ... // IWYU pragma: export` line in X (common/json.hpp:5 exports nlohmann::json).
   Uses: `git -C WT show HEAD:F | grep -n -w -E 'NAME1|NAME2|...' | grep -v '#include'`. Zero = item. A use under `#ifdef` counts as a use (that case belongs to debug-switch-or-output-left-on).
   Already used at BASE: `git -C WT show BASE:F | grep -n -w -E 'NAME1|...'`. Every name already used there = the include changed nothing that compiles; ask what it is for, minor ('what does this #include get us?', 2729005716: BASE b604cb860a model.hpp used fmt::format_string at :639, :654, :669 before bundled/core.h entered at :20).
   Body reason: `gh pr view N --json body -q .body | grep -n -i -F 'X'`; a body line that names the include with its reason ('header hygiene (<cmath>, <cstdlib>)', PR 2646) is the author's answer, do not ask again.
   Move history, both directions: `git -C WT log --format='%h %s' --no-merges BASE..HEAD -- F` and `git -C WT show --stat <commit>`; a commit that removes more than half of F's lines while creating a new file (PR 1920: dd2ced785b, t/t_hwattention.cpp -466, t/t_hwattention_replay.cpp +524) marks every zero-use include or alias in F as 'left over from the move to <new file>'. Keep `git -C WT log --format='%h %s' BASE..HEAD -- X` and `git -C WT log --format=%h -S'NAME' BASE..HEAD -- X` for the header-shrank case (PR 1997: 735a4ffb2d moved relerr/abserr/comberr out of bf16.hpp).
   Duplicates: `git -C WT show HEAD:F | grep '^#include' | sort | uniq -d`; then `git -C WT log --format='%h %p %s' -S'#include "X"' BASE..HEAD -- F` and call it a merge artifact only when the commit that added the second copy has two parents; otherwise name the commit (PR 1920: model.hpp `#include "pos/lib.hpp"` at :19 and :29, added by 11cbfa723a, one parent).
   An alias with zero uses in its file follows the same use grep (`git -C WT show HEAD:F | grep -c -w ALIAS` minus 1).
6. Added parameter: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^@@ -[0-9]+,0 \+[0-9]+ @@ .*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*\(' -A1 | grep -E '^[0-9]+-\+\s+[A-Za-z_:<>&* ]+ [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*,?$'` (a hunk that adds lines and removes none, whose `@@` context names a function, whose added line is a parameter declaration); take FUNC from the `@@` context (PR 2233, BASE de8081fac4 HEAD af9438799a: `@@ -241,0 +260 @@ extern void fill_attn_job_template(` with `+    const std::vector<shard_layer_t>& shards,`). Then `git -C WT grep -n 'FUNC(' HEAD -- h src t`, record the argument at each call, and `git -C WT grep -n -E 'FIELD =|->FIELD\[' HEAD -- h src` for the later writer of the field the parameter fills (work_req->nshards written again at self_attention.hpp:634-640).
7. Branches and statements. Candidates: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^\+\s*if \('` (PR 1920: 29). Keep only those whose condition is a bool field, flag or enum compare that also appears in an `if` of the same function at HEAD; read those by hand, walking the braces outward (`git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk -v L=LINE 'NR<=L && /^\s*(if|\} else|else)/ {print NR": "$0}' | tail -8` is a candidate list, not a verdict; it does not track nesting). `git -C WT diff -U3 BASE HEAD | grep -n -A3 -E 'ASSERT\(false|std::unreachable|abort\('` for a statement after an always-failing assert (TRON_ASSERT is `if tron_unlikely (!(cond)) tron_abort(...)` at h/common/assert.hpp:69-74, and assert.hpp:3-4 undefines NDEBUG). `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -n 'TRACE_EVENT_END("SPAN")'` for a second end of one span (cef0fb5b64:src/pos/worker.cpp:775 unconditional and :777 under `#ifdef PERFETTO_CMD_WDS_LOG`; at d4d6524dd5 one remains). For a declaration above `#ifdef X`: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n "$((L)),$((L+20))p" | grep -n NAME` and the whole file for uses after the block.
8. Touched headers: `for f in $(git -C WT diff --name-only BASE HEAD -- 'h/*.hpp'); do b=$(basename $f); c=$(git -C WT grep -l -E "#include .*$b" HEAD -- h src t bin ingest | grep -v "^HEAD:$f$" | wc -l); printf "%-40s includers=%s\n" "$f" "$c"; done`. Zero = nothing compiles the hunk; say whether the PR adds an includer later (3a8544cd35:t/t_gof_staging_leaks.cpp:43 `// IWYU pragma: keep`).
9. Lift test: `gh pr view N --json title,body -q '.title + " " + .body' | grep -n -i -E 'step [0-9]|first step|second step|third step|phase [0-9]|first phase|lifts?\b|pulls? in|merge of|from the [a-z_-]+ branch|originally authored by'`. One hit plus a named source branch (hwattention_sync, bill-attn-merge) = lift PR. Minor-tier items (unused constant, unused include, zero-caller helper with no promise, member with no reader, prototype with neither caller nor definition) fold into one 'fwiw' line listing the names and confirming they exist on the source branch (`git -C WT grep -w NAME origin/<branch>`). Normal-tier items still fire.
10. Report one item per name, include, parameter or branch; chain follow-ups in the same file ('and this?', 'same here') under the first item. Cite the commit Wade's comment was made on, not the corpus `commit` field (2915258232 and 2915281835 show 8f22c93862 but the state exists at 4491ff73db; 3463077403 shows 39396c8728 but the missing definition exists at 4d2a3951e7).

On PR 2903 (HEAD 64ea13a671 at the comment, BASE 947d045a14): step 2 lists inwork_ring_size consumers=1, max_cmd_fifo_depth consumers=1, short_timeout_ns consumers=0 (h/pos/config.hpp:49 `inline constexpr uint64_t short_timeout_ns = 1000;`, sibling timeout_ns at :46); at b8739108f7 (final head) `git grep -w short_timeout_ns` returns nothing (author: "no longer used. removed"). Step 5 on the same PR: pos/minfifo.hpp, <atomic>, <cstddef>, <cstdint> and common/assert.hpp have consumers in their files (device.hpp:265, minfifo.hpp:66/:73 and :34/:49/:71, driver.cpp:76, minfifo.cpp:9); no duplicate lines and no merge commit. h/pos/device.hpp:7 `#include <thread>` has no thread symbol in the file at 64ea13a671 or at b8739108f7 (only comments at :263/:266 and `pthread_barrier_t` at :581), so step 5 flags one include Wade did not raise; he did flag the standard header <fstream> on PR 1920, so no standard-header exemption is supported and this hit is recorded as an unraised step-5 result.
On PR 1920 (HEAD 2d53016b44, BASE b604cb860a = base.sha): step 1 with the column-0 regex gives exactly 13 functions; step 2 gives callers=0 for exactly dump_kv_cache_from_hbm (h/pos/hwattention.hpp:1145) and dump_qkv_data (:1177), 1 to 5 for the other 11. Step 5 on t/t_hwattention.cpp: <fstream> (:2), common/json.hpp (:13) and `using json = nlohmann::json;` (:27) have zero uses while t/t_hwattention_replay.cpp uses std::ifstream at :129, :234, :328, :378 and the same alias at :27; `git log --no-merges BASE..HEAD -- t/t_hwattention.cpp` lists dd2ced785b "break the replay test out into it's own test file as t_hwattention_replay". model.hpp:20 bundled/core.h: fmt:: used at HEAD :643-676 and :1376, and already at BASE :639, :654, :669 without the include (2729005716). Step 5 also lists the duplicate `#include "pos/lib.hpp"` in model.hpp (:19, :29; 11cbfa723a, one parent), which Wade did not post.
On PR 2287 (HEAD c459e255d9): callers=0 for clear_kv_complete (h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:560) and >=1 for mark_k_complete, mark_v_complete, is_kv_complete; step 3 hits 'called between forward passes' at :559. On PR 4007 (HEAD 29a39ac33e): step 8 gives h/pos/hwattention.hpp includers=18, h/pos/hwattention_dump.hpp includers=0.
Silent-PR probe 2026-10-06: tron-3756 (36 files), tron-2875, tron-2135, tron-2774 produce no item; tron-4353 produced two only through the paren grep and the wide regex (base_load, inverse_speed), zero with the column-0 regex and `-w`; tron-1707, tron-1722, tron-2646 (lift PRs) produce 17 minor-tier items that step 9 folds into one fwiw line each.
final.widen_delta: New check 14, not a widening of an existing one. Check 10 asks whether a hunk belongs to the feature (its candidate test needs removed BASE lines, so a pure addition never qualifies); check 12 asks for owner sign-off on a header change (its unobserved-guarantee half needs a comment that says a revert is undetectable). Neither searches for a consumer of a declared name, an include, a parameter or a header, nor for a missing definition. Count 21 comments over 12 PRs. The agent-run procedure reproduced Wade's item on PR 2903 (short_timeout_ns) plus one hit he did not post (device.hpp:7 <thread>, step 5); on PR 1920 it reproduced dump_kv_cache_from_hbm and dump_qkv_data, the three t_hwattention.cpp leftovers and the bundled/core.h question (after the BASE comparison was added), plus one unposted duplicate include in model.hpp; on PR 2287 clear_kv_complete; on PR 4007 hwattention_dump.hpp with 0 includers. On eight silent PRs it fires only on three lift PRs, which the lift rule folds into one 'fwiw' line each. The setup line changes for this check: BASE is the PR's base.sha, not the merge-base, because merged heads return themselves. The description line of SKILL.md gains "symbols, includes and parameters with no consumer, declarations with no definition, branches an enclosing guard already fixes" and the thirteen questions become fourteen.
